subject: Secure hosting discovery & residency checklist — next steps
messages:
From: Claire Nguyen <claire@medaxis.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: Thomas Lee <thomas.lee@medaxis.com>
Date: 2028-07-10 14:22 -0400
Subject: Follow-up / hosting constraints from today's discovery

Thanks for today's call, Dylan — appreciate the clear overview. I wanted to capture the constraints we discussed so your team can propose a concrete POC scope. High-level pain points and constraints from our side:

- Data residency: All patient data must remain in EU-controlled infrastructure; primary region should be Frankfurt (eu-central-1).
- Air-gap requirement: For core PHI workflows we need an isolated on-prem or fully air-gapped deployment option; limited outbound egress (approval-only).
- Control plane: We cannot route customer data through a shared public control plane unless we have a contractual data flow guarantee and proof of separation (audit logs).
- Network: Strict firewall rules; only whitelisted IPs; we prefer static outbound IPs for allowlisting to partner services.
- KMS/HSM: Customer-managed key material is mandatory for the PHI dataset; prefer KMIP or AWS CloudHSM integrations.
- Compliance artifacts: SOC 2 evidence and penetration test report will be required for procurement review.

Actions requested from Redwood: please confirm minimal port list, any connector agents required for on-prem, sample network diagram, and a one-page summary of the Private offering that we can share with our procurement and security teams.

I've attached a simple network diagram sketch we used on the call (medaxis-network-diagram.pdf). Thomas from procurement is looped in; he'll own timeline/budget.

Thanks,
Claire
Director, IT Security
MedAxis, Inc.

Attachment: medaxis-network-diagram.pdf (PDF, 420KB)

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Nguyen <claire@medaxis.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Thomas Lee <thomas.lee@medaxis.com>
Date: 2028-07-11 09:08 -0400
Subject: Re: Follow-up / hosting constraints from today's discovery

Claire — thanks for the clear summary and for the diagram. Quick recap from our side to make sure we're aligned, then proposed next steps.

Pain points we heard (short):
- EU-only residency for PHI workflows
- Need an isolated/private deployment pattern (on-prem or air-gapped) with customer-managed keys
- Strict firewall/allowlist requirements and no uncontrolled egress
- Procurement will require SOC 2 + pen test artifacts and a short technical statement for legal

Redwood Private options that match:
- Private VPC with a customer-managed control plane (redwood private) in Frankfurt, OR
- On-prem agent + air-gapped runtime: we can ship a deployable runtime bundle to run in your air-gapped environment with an ops playbook.

Technical asks we'll need from MedAxis to size/propose a POC:
1) Expected peak concurrent inference load (requests/min and token length distribution)
2) Approx dataset size for hosted model cache + retention expectations
3) Whether you require an HSM (yes/no) and preferred vendor/protocol (KMIP/CloudHSM)
4) Egress and inbound port constraints (we'll propose minimal ports below)

Immediate deliverables from Redwood (we will send by EOD tomorrow):
- Minimal ports and IP ranges document (redwood-private-ports.pdf)
- A one-page Private deployment summary for procurement
- Draft SOW template for a 4-week POC (mdx-poc-sow.docx)

Ports summary (high level):
- 443 (HTTPS) outbound for attestations and optional control plane telemetry (can be blocked for air-gapped)
- 22 (SSH) only for initial troubleshooting (optional, can be replaced by jump-host)
- 5671/5672 or custom messaging port for internal RPC if using on-prem connector

Notes on KMS/HSM: We support CloudHSM and customer-managed KMS via PKCS11/KMIP integrations. If you insist on no external key escrow, we can broker an HSM-only flow with local key wrapping.

Next steps I propose:
- Ben Carter (SE) will schedule a 60-minute technical deep dive next week to review the diagram and POC network requirements.
- We'll deliver the three documents attached to help procurement.

I've attached the ports doc and a draft SOW. Ben, Monica — please take point on scheduling.

Best,
Dylan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-private-ports.pdf (PDF, 28KB); mdx-poc-sow.docx (DOCX, 12KB)

From: Claire Nguyen <claire@medaxis.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: Thomas Lee <thomas.lee@medaxis.com>
Date: 2028-07-12 11:46 +02:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up / hosting constraints from today's discovery

Thank you — that is exactly the level of detail procurement/security asked for. Quick clarifications:
- We have a projected steady-state of ~25 req/s with occasional spikes to 60 req/s; average prompt size ~450 tokens.
- PHI dataset for caching: ~220GB. Retention policy: 30 days rolling.
- We will require HSM backed keys for any model that sees PHI. We use a vendor that supports KMIP.

Thomas has asked whether Redwood can provide a short statement that we can include in our security questionnaire describing the data flow and whether PII/PHI ever traverses Redwood control plane. Can you prepare a 2-3 sentence statement confirming: 1) primary data paths, 2) whether telemetry can be disabled, and 3) whether customer keys remain under our control?

Thomas will own procurement scheduling — he prefers a two-week procurement window after the POC demo.

Claire

To: Claire Nguyen <claire@medaxis.com>, Thomas Lee <thomas.lee@medaxis.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-15 09:05 -0400
Subject: Re: Follow-up / hosting constraints from today's discovery — next steps and statement

Claire / Thomas — thanks for the numbers and clarifications. Per your ask, a concise statement you can use in the security questionnaire follows (feel free to paste into your doc):

"Redwood Inference operates a configurable Private deployment model. For MedAxis POC and production configurations, customer data and inference payloads remain within the customer-designated infrastructure (Frankfurt region or on-premises) and do not persist in Redwood's shared hosted control plane. Telemetry and control-plane telemetry can be disabled per customer policy; any optional telemetry is sent over TLS to customer-approved endpoints. Customer-managed keys (KMIP/CloudHSM) are supported and can be used such that Redwood does not have access to unwrapped key material."

Planned next steps from Redwood: 
- SE deep dive: Ben Carter will reach out to schedule an engineering call (60 min) to validate network diagram and ports.
- Deliverables: final ports doc + 1-pager + draft SOW by EOD 7/15 (linked in Drive).
- POC scope: 4-week on-prem POC focusing on model latency at 99th percentile and secure key integration; milestone: demo + procurement handoff.

Ben / Monica — please confirm availability for the deep dive. Thomas, what's your preferred day/time for the engineering call?

Thanks,
Dylan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
